					306 text A GitHub monorepo subpath identifies one tool, but the signing identity is still pinned to the repository. The signed project and version must match the requested tool and release, regardless of the bundle's filename. For a domain project, obtain the vendor's public key through a trusted channel and configure it explicitly. This example assumes the key file already exists:
					307 button Copy Code
					308 text TOML
					309 container
						310 text [ tools ] "packslip:tool.example.com" = { version =  "latest" , pubkey =  "/path/to/vendor.pub"  }
					311 text The domain's signed list points to release bundles; their artifacts can live on a different download host. A domain project without a signed list cannot be installed. Recognizing a forge's signing issuer does not provide discovery: GitHub has a release-API integration; other hosts need the signed-list location.
					312 heading Versions Permalink to "Versions", Value: 2, ID: versions
						313 text Versions
						314 link Description: Permalink to "Versions", Value: …
					315 text List the project's available versions with:
					316 button Copy Code
					317 text SH
					318 container
						319 text mise  ls-remote  packslip:github.com/jdx/packslip
					320 text Packslip versions use semver, including compatible date versions such as 
					321 text 2026.9.1
					322 text . mise uses that version to order releases and identify prereleases; GitHub's release order and editable prerelease flag do not decide either. Prereleases are excluded unless the 
					323 text prerelease
					324 text  tool option is enabled. For GitHub discovery, mise reads versions from tags such as 
					325 text v1.2.3
					326 text , 
					327 text mytool-v1.2.3
					328 text , or 
					329 text v4.1
					330 text  (normalized to 
					331 text 4.1.0
					332 text ). Tags that do not map to a version need an explicit mapping in a signed list. At installation, the manifest's version must agree with the tag or list entry.
					333 heading Signed release lists Permalink to "Signed release lists", Value: 3, ID: signed-release-lists
						334 text Signed release lists
						335 link Description: Permalink to "Signed release lists", Value: …
					336 text A GitHub repository can publish a supplementary signed list on its default branch at 
					337 text .well-known/packslip.json
					338 text , or 
					339 text .well-known/packslip/<tool>.json
					340 text  for a monorepo tool. The list can withdraw a version, supply a bundle URL and digest, or add a version that the release API does not expose. Omitted versions can still come from GitHub releases: omission does not withdraw them. For a domain project, the signed list supplies the entire release index. A vendor withdrawal excludes a version even if a trusted stamper approved it.
					341 heading Release-list continuity and minimum age Permalink to "Release-list continuity and minimum age", Value: 3, ID: release-list-continuity-and-minimum-age
						342 text Release-list continuity and minimum age
						343 link Description: Permalink to "Release-list continuity and minimum age", Value: …
					344 text mise rejects expired signed lists and sequences below the highest it has accepted for the project. Once it has accepted a supplementary GitHub list, that list disappearing is an error. A missing list cannot silently undo a withdrawal. This continuity state is stored alongside the 
					345 link Description: signer pin, Value: …
					346 text . If a 
					347 link Description: minimum release age, Value: …
					348 text  is configured, discovery timestamps help filter candidates. Before downloading an artifact, mise checks the verified transparency-log timestamp against the effective cutoff. Only an explicitly allowed unlogged bundle uses the signed publication timestamp instead.
					349 heading Latest Permalink to "Latest", Value: 2, ID: latest
						350 text Latest
						351 link Description: Permalink to "Latest", Value: …
					352 text An unconstrained 
					353 text latest
					354 text  request considers recommendations in this order:
					355 content list
						356 container
							357 AXListMarker 1. 
							358 text The vendor's  latest  pointer in an accepted signed release list.
						359 container
							360 AXListMarker 2. 
							361 text GitHub's latest release, if there is no signed pointer.
						362 container
							363 AXListMarker 3. 
							364 text The highest eligible semver, if there is no eligible recommendation.
					365 text The vendor can recommend an older supported release while a newer major version exists. Prefix and channel requests keep their normal matching rules; the recommendation does not reorder them. A recommendation must still pass signature, identity, digest, release-age, stamping, and host checks. A policy exclusion warns and tries another candidate. An ineligible signed recommendation falls directly back to semver selection, without consulting GitHub's pointer. Signature or digest failures and invalid, expired, rolled-back, or unexpectedly missing lists stop resolution. Version listing and 
					366 text latest
					367 text  resolution perform online policy checks and bypass mise's remote-version cache so withdrawals and trust changes take effect.
					368 heading What is verified Permalink to "What is verified", Value: 2, ID: what-is-verified
						369 text What is verified
						370 link Description: Permalink to "What is verified", Value: …
					371 text Before unpacking a release, mise checks:
					372 content list
						373 container
							374 AXListMarker 1. 
							375 text The bundle's signature and applicable certificate and transparency-log evidence against the expected repository identity or configured key.
						376 container
							377 AXListMarker 2. 
							378 text The statement's structure, requested project and version, and any bundle digest recorded by a vendor list or trusted stamper.
						379 container
							380 AXListMarker 3. 
							381 text Signer continuity, lockfile commitments, and applicable release-age policy.
						382 container
							383 AXListMarker 4. 
							384 text The selected artifact's digest and size, plus any existing lockfile checksum.
					385 text The verified statement is retained as 
					386 text .mise-packslip.json
					387 text  in the install directory. It supplies executable paths and metadata for resources. Verification authenticates the signer's statement and the downloaded bytes. It does not establish that the software is safe. A provenance link in the manifest is separate evidence: this backend records its presence for continuity checks but does not fetch and verify the linked build provenance.
					388 heading Artifact selection Permalink to "Artifact selection", Value: 3, ID: artifact-selection
						389 text Artifact selection
						390 link Description: Permalink to "Artifact selection", Value: …
					391 text mise uses signed metadata to select one artifact:
					392 content list
						393 container
							394 AXListMarker 1. 
							395 text Match OS, architecture, and libc. An absent field leaves only that dimension unrestricted: a universal macOS build still requires macOS.
						396 container
							397 AXListMarker 2. 
							398 text With a  variant , consider only that variant. Without one, consider only artifacts that have no variant.
						399 container
							400 AXListMarker 3. 
							401 text Keep formats mise can install, preferring the most specific platform match, then its archive/compression format preference over a bare executable.
						402 container
							403 AXListMarker 4. 
							404 text Refuse an unresolved tie rather than guessing between builds.
					405 text Installer formats such as 
					406 text deb
					407 text , 
					408 text dmg
					409 text , and 
					410 text msi
					411 text  are not selected. A glibc host with no matching GNU artifact may use a musl artifact; mise reports that fallback in the debug log. The vendor must distinguish alternative builds with variants; a client-side option cannot repair two identically described artifacts.
					412 heading Host requirements Permalink to "Host requirements", Value: 2, ID: host-requirements
						413 text Host requirements
						414 link Description: Permalink to "Host requirements", Value: …
					415 text After selecting an artifact, mise checks its declared requirements before downloading it. Requirements do not break a selection tie or select another build.
					416 table
						417 row
							418 cell
								419 text REQUIREMENT RESULT
							420 cell
								421 text MISE BEHAVIOR
						422 row
							423 cell
								424 text Confirmed missing library, insufficient glibc, or insufficient OS version
							425 cell
								426 text Refuse installation.
						427 row
							428 cell
								429 text Missing or outdated required command
							430 cell
								431 text Warn and continue.
						432 row
							433 cell
								434 text A check cannot be completed
							435 cell
								436 text Warn instead of assuming the host is incompatible.
					437 text Command checks prefer active mise tools over ambient PATH. Library detection is platform-dependent; for example, an absent macOS library file may still exist in the dyld shared cache, so mise reports that absence as unknown.
					438 text ignore_requirements = true
					439 text  allows a tool to install despite confirmed failures. It does not supply the missing libraries or make an incompatible executable run.
					440 heading Pinned signers Permalink to "Pinned signers", Value: 2, ID: pinned-signers
						441 text Pinned signers
						442 link Description: Permalink to "Pinned signers", Value: …
					443 text mise preserves trust in two places:
					444 table
						445 row
							446 cell
								447 text STATE
							448 cell
								449 text WHAT IT PROTECTS
						450 row
							451 cell
								452 text packslip/pins.toml
								453 text  under the 
								454 link Description: state directory, Value: …
							455 cell
								456 text Previously accepted signers, signing scheme, vendor versus repackager status, provenance-link presence, and release-list continuity.
						457 row
							458 cell
								459 text mise.lock
							460 cell
								461 text The project's signer and attestor commitment alongside each platform's artifact URL and checksum, including on another machine's first install.
					462 text For a keyless signer, continuity compares the workflow path without its tag or branch ref. A new release tag of the same workflow is the same signer. A new workflow path or key requires an explicit trust decision. A signing-scheme change, a vendor-to-repackager change, or lost provenance links can also be refused. Inspect the local pins before investigating a trust failure:
					463 button Copy Code
					464 text SH
					465 container
						466 text mise  packslip  pins mise  packslip  pins  --json
					467 text After confirming a vendor's announced signer change, reset its local pin:
					468 button Copy Code
					469 text SH
					470 container
						471 text mise  packslip  forget  github.com/owner/repo
					472 text This also resets remembered vendor-list continuity. It does not change an explicit 
					473 text pubkey
					474 text  or identity option, erase stamper-list state, or remove the signer commitment in 
					475 text mise.lock
					476 text . Review those separately when accepting a rotation. A conflicting lockfile entry must be removed and regenerated after the new policy is configured; commit the reviewed change for other machines.
					477 heading Stamps Permalink to "Stamps", Value: 2, ID: stamps
						478 text Stamps
						479 link Description: Permalink to "Stamps", Value: …
					480 text A stamper is a registry, mirror, or review service that publishes a signed list of releases it admits. Configure the hosts you trust and the key or identity allowed to sign each host's lists:
					481 button Copy Code
					482 text TOML
					483 container
						484 text [ settings . packslip ] stampers = [   "stamps.example.com=/path/to/stamper.pub" ,   "reviews.example.com=https://github.com/example/reviews/" , ]
					485 text Each entry is 
					486 text host=PIN
					487 text . The pin may be a minisign-format public key line, a public-key file path, or a GitHub identity prefix. The example hosts and key path are placeholders; replace them with a service and pin you trust. A host publishes one list per project at 
					488 text https://<host>/.well-known/packslip/<project>.json
					489 text . With stampers configured:
					490 content list
						491 container
							492 AXListMarker • 
							493 text A version needs a non-yanked approval from at least one trusted host to be listed or installed. One host's withdrawal does not veto another's approval.
						494 container
							495 AXListMarker • 
							496 text A vendor withdrawal still excludes the release, regardless of stamps.
						497 container
							498 AXListMarker • 
							499 text mise checks the stamped bundle digest and the vendor-list digest, when present, then verifies the vendor signature. A stamp never replaces that signature.
						500 container
							501 AXListMarker • 
							502 text Expired, rolled-back, invalid, or previously accepted but now missing stamper lists cause errors. Silently ignoring one would weaken the configured policy.
					503 text A stamper can mirror the exact vendor-signed bundle. Re-signed repackager bundles requiring a separate identity policy are not supported here. No stamps are required when the setting is unset. To exempt one tool from configured stampers, set 
					504 text trust = "vendor"
					505 text  as described below.
					506 heading Tool Options Permalink to "Tool Options", Value: 2, ID: tool-options
						507 text Tool Options
						508 link Description: Permalink to "Tool Options", Value: …
					509 text These 
					510 link Description: tool options, Value: …
					511 text  go in 
					512 text [tools]
					513 text  in 
					514 text mise.toml
					515 text . They apply to one tool; 
					516 text packslip.exec
					517 text , 
					518 text packslip.stampers
					519 text , and 
					520 text skills.*
					521 text  are settings and belong under 
					522 text [settings]
					523 text .
					524 heading variant Permalink to "`variant`", Value: 3, ID: variant
						525 text variant
						526 link Description: Permalink to "`variant`", Value: …
					527 text Choose a vendor-declared alternative build, such as 
					528 text fips
					529 text  or 
					530 text baseline
					531 text . Without this option, only unvarianted builds are considered.

						535 text [ tools ] "packslip:github.com/example/tool" = { version =  "latest" , variant =  "fips"  }

						537 text pubkey
						538 link Description: Permalink to "`pubkey`", Value: …
					539 text Pin a key-signed release using the minisign-format public-key line or a path to its 
					540 text .pub
					541 text  file. The vendor list and release bundles must verify against it.
					542 heading identity, identity_prefix, issuer Permalink to "`identity`, `identity_prefix`, `issuer`", Value: 3, ID: identity-identity-prefix-issuer

						545 text identity_prefix

					549 text Pin a keyless signer using an exact certificate identity or an identity prefix, plus its OIDC issuer. These options can replace the policy derived from a forge name. Keep the trailing slash when pinning a repository prefix.
					550 heading allow_unlogged Permalink to "`allow_unlogged`", Value: 3, ID: allow-unlogged
						551 text allow_unlogged
						552 link Description: Permalink to "`allow_unlogged`", Value: …
					553 text Defaults to 
					554 text false
					555 text . Set to 
					556 text true
					557 text  only when your policy accepts a vendor's key-signed bundles without transparency-log evidence. This does not bypass signature or artifact verification.
					558 heading trust Permalink to "`trust`", Value: 3, ID: trust
						559 text trust
						560 link Description: Permalink to "`trust`", Value: …
					561 text trust = "vendor"
					562 text  exempts the tool from configured stampers while retaining vendor signature verification. The choice is recorded in lockfile options.

						568 text prerelease

					570 text Set to

						574 text ignore_requirements

					576 text Set to

					666 heading Why publish one Permalink to "Why publish one", Value: 2, ID: why-publish-one
						667 text Why publish one
						668 link Description: Permalink to "Why publish one", Value: …
					669 text A packslip lets a vendor describe each release's platforms and executable paths with the release itself. Users can install through 
					670 text packslip:
					671 text  without a new registry shorthand or a separate filename-matching recipe. It can also supply versioned completions, CLI specifications, and agent skills. The 
					672 text github:
